channel.title: Deep Dive: Embodied Consciousness & Neural Computation
channel.itunes:author: Matthew S. Yorek
channel.itunes:summary: Embodied consciousness, synaptic bioenergetics, clinical disorders of consciousness, stroke syndromes, anesthesia dynamics, and living human neurons vs. artificial neural networks.
channel.description: Embodied consciousness, synaptic bioenergetics, clinical disorders of consciousness, stroke syndromes, anesthesia dynamics, and living human neurons vs. artificial neural networks.

image.title: Deep Dive: Embodied Consciousness & Neural Computation

item.title: How an Eye-Pressure Test Reads Through the Cornea — Schiøtz Indentation, Goldmann & Schmidt's 1957 3.06-mm Applanation Tear-Film & Corneal Stiffness Balance, Ehlers's Cannulated Eye Study & OHTS Corneal Thickness
item.description: Biomechanics of intraocular pressure measurement through the cornea (H052): Schiøtz (1905) indentation vs. Goldmann & Schmidt's (1957) small-area 3.06-mm applanation balancing tear-film capillarity against corneal stiffness, Ehlers et al.'s (1975) direct intracameral manometry demonstrating corneal thickness bias, and OHTS (2002) risk stratification.

item.title: The Switch That Keeps Us Awake — Hypothalamic Orexin/Hypocretin Discovery, Canine HCRTR2 & Human CSF Orexin-A Deficiency in Narcolepsy Type 1, OX2R Crystal Structures (4S0V/7L1U) & Dual Orexin Receptor Antagonists
item.description: From wake-maintenance physiology to targeted insomnia pharmacology: 1998 discovery of hypothalamic hypocretins/orexins, 1999 canine HCRTR2 and murine knockout narcolepsy models, human CSF orexin-A <=110 pg/mL cutoff in ICSD-3 narcolepsy type 1, structural comparison of antagonist-bound (PDB 4S0V) vs. agonist-bound (PDB 7L1U) OX2R, and clinical trials and next-morning safety of suvorexant and daridorexant.

item.title: The Sedative the Screen Missed — GABAA alpha1-beta2-gamma2 Cryo-EM Allosteric Binding (6X3X/6X3U), Diazepam CYP2C19/3A4 vs. Lorazepam Direct UGT2B15 Glucuronidation & Why Urine Immunoassays Miss Lorazepam-Glucuronide
item.description: Receptor allostery, metabolic routing, and toxicology screen blind spots: cryo-EM structures of human alpha1-beta2-gamma2 GABAA receptors bound to diazepam (PDB 6X3X) and flumazenil (PDB 6X3U), Sternbach's benzodiazepine chemistry, diazepam CYP oxidation vs. lorazepam direct C3-OH glucuronidation, and why unhydrolyzed urine benzodiazepine immunoassays miss lorazepam-glucuronide without beta-glucuronidase hydrolysis and LC-MS/MS.

item.title: When the Same Taste Signal Leads to Opposite Choices — Chandrashekar's Dish Bitter Receptor Screen, Zhao & Mueller's RASSL Spiradoline Routing & Human TAS2R16 Expressed in Mouse Sweet vs. Bitter Cells
item.description: Labeled-line coding in mammalian taste: separating molecular ligand detection in heterologous cells (Chandrashekar et al. 2000; Bufe et al. 2002 TAS2R16) from behavioral attraction vs. aversion in mice when the exact same engineered receptor (spiradoline RASSL, Zhao 2003) or human bitter receptor (TAS2R16, Mueller 2005) is expressed in T1R2 sweet cells vs. T2R bitter cells.

item.title: How an Audiogram Finds Which Ear Heard the Tone — Fletcher & Wegel's 1922 Calibrated Thresholds, Transcranial Bone-Conduction Crossover, Denes & Naunton's Narrowband Noise & Hood's 1957 Masking Plateau
item.description: Acoustics and clinical logic of pure-tone audiometry and contralateral masking (H050): Fletcher & Wegel's (1922) calibrated receiver thresholds, skull-vibration crossover to the non-test cochlea, Denes & Naunton's (1952) frequency-band masking efficiency, and J.D. Hood's (1957) plateau method separating cross-heard responses from true ear-specific air- and bone-conduction thresholds.

item.title: The Breakfast That Changed a Bargain — Controlled 850-kcal Breakfast Crossovers in Ultimatum Bargaining (Strang 2017) vs. fMRI Risk Lotteries (Liu 2021), Plasma Tyrosine/LNAA & Human Tyrosine Hydroxylase Cryo-EM (6ZZU/6ZVP)
item.description: How acute macronutrient swaps in controlled 850-kcal breakfasts affect distinct economic decision tasks: Strang et al.'s (2017) Ultimatum Game crossover (unfair-offer rejection and plasma tyrosine/LNAA AUC) vs. Liu et al.'s (2021) fMRI monetary lottery crossover (overall behavioral null, fat-mass interaction, tryptophan/LNAA correlation, and parietal BOLD thresholds), grounded in human tyrosine hydroxylase cryo-EM structures (PDB 6ZZU apo & 6ZVP dopamine-bound).

item.title: How a Sea Slug Gets Used to a Touch — Pinsker's Aplysia Gill-Withdrawal Habituation, Castellucci & Kandel's 1974 Quantal Failure Analysis & Bailey & Chen's Electron-Microscopy Presynaptic Active Zones
item.description: From behavioral habituation to synaptic quantal release and ultrastructure in Aplysia: Pinsker et al.'s (1970) gill-withdrawal habituation and dishabituation, Castellucci & Kandel's (1974) quantal variance/failure proof that short-term habituation reflects fewer transmitter packets released per impulse rather than smaller postsynaptic unit responses, and Bailey & Chen's (1983) electron microscopy of long-term habituated sensory-neuron varicosities.

item.title: The Drug That Changed the Ward — Chlorpromazine from Rhône-Poulenc Patent & 1952 Psychiatric Wards (Laborit, Delay & Elkes) to Pause-Triggered Torsades, Human hERG Cryo-EM (5VA1), DRD2 Kinetics & Sulfoxide LC-MS/MS
item.description: Two ward records seventy years apart: chlorpromazine's transition from Rhône-Poulenc synthesis (US2645640A) and Laborit's 1952 surgical 'artificial hibernation' to Delay & Deniker's psychiatric cases, Elkes & Elkes's 1954 crossover, and the 1964 NIMH Collaborative Study, paired with a contemporary pause-triggered torsades workup (Fridericia QTc 531 ms), ligand-free human hERG cryo-EM (PDB 5VA1), oocyte vs. CHO IC50s (21.6 vs. 1.47 µM), and DRD2 residence kinetics.

item.title: The Pause That Finally Had a Time — Implantable Loop Recorder Asystole Masquerading as Epilepsy (Kanjwal 2010) vs. 38-Second Ictal Asystole on Simultaneous EEG/ECG (Nandkeolyar 2018), RAST Yield & Recorder Artifacts
item.description: Behind the Curtain of ambulatory ECG and implantable loop recording (H041): Kanjwal et al.'s (2010) loop-recorder capture of complete heart block and prolonged asystole causing convulsive syncope previously treated as epilepsy, contrasted with Nandkeolyar et al.'s (2018) simultaneous video-EEG/ECG capture of right temporal seizure onset preceding a 38-second ictal asystole, Krahn's randomized RAST diagnostic yield (14/27 vs. 6/30), and Domenichini's (2023) false-positive pause artifacts.

item.title: How a Locust Turns Sound into Current — Michelsen's Abdominal Frequency Tuning, Windmill's Laser-Scanned Tympanum Waves, Warren's Auditory Receptor Currents & Chaiyasitdhi's 2-µm Axial Pull vs. Push
item.description: Biophysics of insect tympanal hearing in the desert locust: Michelsen's (1968) receptor frequency tuning, Windmill et al.'s (2008) laser-vibrometry frequency-sorting waves across the abdominal tympanum, Warren & Matheson's (2018) isolated transduction currents, and Chaiyasitdhi et al.'s (2025 reviewed preprint) direct 2-µm cap pull vs. push recordings.

item.title: Why a Fly's Eye Went Quiet in the Light — Cosens & Manning's 1969 Drosophila trp Mutant, Montell's Gene Rescue, Hardie & Minke's Ca2+-Selective Current, Niemeyer's trp/trpl Double Mutant & Asp621 Pore Selectivity
item.description: Discovery of the founding TRP ion channel in Drosophila vision: Cosens & Manning's (1969) transient receptor potential mutant fading in continuous light, Montell & Rubin's gene rescue and cloning, Hardie & Minke's (1992) single-photoreceptor patch-clamp proof of missing Ca2+ permeability, Niemeyer et al.'s (1996) trp/trpl dissection, and Liu et al.'s (2007) pore-selectivity mutagenesis.

item.title: The Click With No Trace — Canine Unilateral BAER Deafness (Plonek English Setter & Lewis 8,955 UK Dalmatians) vs. Pediatric Auditory Neuropathy Recovery with Normal Speech & Absent Click ABR
item.description: Comparative auditory diagnostics across species (H050 & V034): Plonek's unilaterally deaf English Setter BAER waveforms and Lewis's 8,955-dog UK Dalmatian screening cohort (1,201 unilateral, 397 bilateral, 8 equivocal) paired with Starr's classic auditory neuropathy series and Eom's child with absent click ABR yet normal pure-tone thresholds and language.

item.title: The Amino Acid at the Brain's Gate — Six-Competitor Plasma Tryptophan Ratio, Human LAT1 Cryo-EM (8J8M/8XPU), TPH2 & PET Tracer Assumptions, Delgado's Remission Relapse Trials (14/21; 8/15 vs. 1/15) & Breakfast Limits
item.description: From plasma amino-acid competition at blood-brain barrier LAT1–CD98hc (PDB 8J8M L-Trp & 8XPU JPH203) to acute tryptophan depletion trials: UHPLC-MS/MS separation of isobaric Leu/Ile, recombinant TPH2 kinetics vs. alpha-[11C]methyl-L-Trp PET assumptions, Delgado's remitted depression crossover (14/21) and SSRI vs. desipramine responder split (8/15 vs. 1/15), and why Wurtman's breakfast study measured plasma ratios rather than mood.

item.title: Epochs, Dipoles, and Saltatory Sparks — Attended Polysomnography, Hypopnea Rules & HSAT Dilution (H044), Scalp & ICU Continuous EEG (H045) & Nerve Conduction Studies and Needle EMG (H046)
item.description: Clinical Cluster & Neurophysiology synthesis of attended polysomnography (H044), scalp/ICU EEG (H045), and NCS/needle EMG (H046): 3% vs. 4% hypopnea rules, pediatric >=2-breath cutoffs, HSAT TRT dilution, RBD synucleinopathy, and CHAT (n=464); 6-10 cm2 cortical dipole threshold, wicket-spike traps, Claassen ICU cEEG (n=570, 92% non-convulsive), and TELSTAR (n=172); and small-fiber blindness, the DRG SNAP law, 10-21 day Wallerian clock, MG vs. LEMS facilitation, cool-limb sodium physics, Martin-Gruber, and Gold Coast ALS criteria.

item.title: Decibels, Diopters, and Millimeters of Mercury — Audiometry, Shadow-Curve Masking, SSCD & NICU ANSD (H050), ETDRS Acuity, Pinhole Optics & Cycloplegic Refraction (H051) & Goldmann 3.06 mm Tonometry, OHTS & Normal-Tension Glaucoma (H052)
item.description: Clinical Cluster & Sensory Biophysics synthesis of audiometry (H050), visual acuity/refraction (H051), and tonometry (H052): unmasked shadow curves, 2 kHz Carhart notch, schwannoma WRS rollover, SSCD stapedial reflex rescue, and NICU OAE+/ABR- ANSD; ETDRS LogMAR, paradoxical pinhole worsening, cycloplegic pseudomyopia, and 20/20 bitemporal hemianopia; and Goldmann 3.06 mm physics, OHTS CCT, post-LASIK PISK, and Tajimi/CNTGS Normal-Tension Glaucoma.

item.title: Reflexes, Recall, and Four Plastic Tubes — Bedside Neurologic Localization & HINTS vs. Early MRI (H053), Cognitive & Neuropsychological Storage-vs-Retrieval Profiling (H054) & Lumbar Puncture, 4-Tube Xanthochromia & CSF Signatures (H055)
item.description: Clinical Cluster & Clinical Neuroscience synthesis of standardized neurologic localization (H053), neuropsychological profiling (H054), and CSF analysis (H055): forehead-sparing CN VII, Romberg proprioception, FOUR Score, HINTS beating early DWI MRI, and Hoover sign; CVLT-3 storage vs. retrieval rescue, DLB haloperidol ban, TOPF norms, and TOMM validity; and Hasbun pre-LP CT + immediate antibiotics, 450-460 nm xanthochromia, CSF lactate, <72h HSV-1 PCR traps, and Lancet 2018 atraumatic needles (n=31,412).

item.title: Tears, Stria Melanocytes, and Spinal Arcs — Veterinary Ophthalmic Exam, Descemetocele 'Donut Hole' & TonoVet Physics (V033), BAER Deafness Screening, MITF/PMEL Stria Collapse & Cavalier PSOM (V034) & Neurologic Localization, Schiff-Sherrington & the Deep Pain Law (V035)
item.description: One Medicine synthesis of veterinary ophthalmology/tonometry (V033), BAER deafness screening (V034), and neurologic localization (V035): STT-I sequence, cherry-eye gland preservation, descemetocele fluorescein 'donut hole', collar/species TonoVet traps, and fellow-eye glaucoma prophylaxis; Strain's >12,000 Dalmatian registry, MITF/KIT stria melanocytes, OFA >=35d rule, and Cavalier PSOM bone BAER; and 4 spinal segments, Schiff-Sherrington, paradoxical vestibular tilt, and Olby's Deep Pain & Progressive Myelomalacia laws.

item.title: When the Same Sound Becomes a Surprise — Sutton's P300 Uncertainty Cue, Bekinschtein's Local-vs.-Global Oddball Hierarchy & Wacongne's Omitted-Tone Prediction Error
item.description: Electrophysiology of auditory expectation and hierarchical prediction error: Sutton et al. (1965) P300 discovery comparing identical clicks under certainty vs. uncertainty, Bekinschtein et al. (2009) local-global paradigm where a locally Deviant XXXXX/XXXXY sequence becomes the global rule, and Wacongne et al. (2011) brain responses to an omitted expected tone.

item.title: How a Burst Leaves a Synapse Stronger — Bliss & Lømo's 1973 Perforant-Path LTP Controls, Collingridge's APV NMDA Blockade & Tsien's CA1-Restricted NR1 Knockout
item.description: Experimental dissection of hippocampal Long-Term Potentiation (LTP): Bliss & Lømo (1973) pathway-specific potentiation lasting hours in rabbit dentate gyrus, Collingridge, Kehl & McLennan (1983) selective NMDA antagonist APV blocking LTP induction while sparing baseline AMPA synaptic transmission, and Tsien, Huerta & Tonegawa (1996) postnatal CA1 NR1 knockout mice.

item.title: When the Lips Change the Sound You Hear — Sumby & Pollack's Speech-in-Noise Gain, McGurk & MacDonald's Ba/Ga→Da Fusion & Beauchamp's Superior Temporal Sulcus TMS Disruption
item.description: Multisensory speech integration and causal cortical testing: Sumby & Pollack (1954) audiovisual enhancement in noise across vocabulary set sizes, McGurk & MacDonald (1976) cross-modal syllable fusion where auditory /ba/ paired with lip-articulated /ga/ yields heard /da/, and Beauchamp, Nath & Pasalar (2010) fMRI-guided TMS over the superior temporal sulcus selectively reducing McGurk fusion while sparing congruent control syllables.

item.title: How a Sour Taste Starts — Huang's PKD2L1 Sour-Cell Ablation, Chang's Apical Proton Current, Tu's Otop1 Proton Channel Cloning & Teng/Zhang's Chorda Tympani Nerve Loss in Otop1-/- Mice
item.description: From cell-type ablation to the molecular proton sensor for sour taste: Huang et al. (2006) selective elimination of PKD2L1 taste cells erasing chorda tympani acid responses while sparing sweet, salty, bitter, and umami, Chang, Waters & Liman (2010) direct measurement of apical proton entry, Tu et al. (2018) discovery of the OTOP1 proton channel, and Teng et al. / Zhang et al. (2019) in vivo Otop1-/- requirement for sour nerve signaling.

item.title: How You Know Where Your Hand Is in the Dark — Goodwin's 100 Hz Tendon-Vibration Illusion, Ghez's Multi-Joint Reaching Without Proprioception, Woo's Piezo2 Spindles & Chesler's Human PIEZO2 Loss
item.description: From psychophysical illusions to the molecular mechanosensor of proprioception: Goodwin, McCloskey & Matthews (1972) tendon-vibration muscle-spindle illusions, Ghez et al. (1995) intersegmental dynamics defects in deafferented human reaching rescued partially by vision, Woo et al. (2015) conditional Piezo2 ablation silencing muscle-spindle Ia afferents, and Chesler et al. (2016) human PIEZO2 deficiency.

item.title: When the Brain Burns Ketones — Drug-Resistant Pediatric Epilepsy, SCOT Succinyl-CoA Transferase (3DLX / 1OOY), [11C]Acetoacetate PET, Decanoate AMPA Block & the Neal Trial
item.description: From the 4:1 ketogenic diet ratio (90% energy from fat) and hepatic HMGCS2 ketogenesis to extrahepatic SCOT/OXCT1 glutamyl-CoA thioester catalysis (human apo PDB 3DLX vs. porcine Glu305 intermediate PDB 1OOY), dual [11C]acetoacetate/[18F]FDG brain PET, Chang et al. (2016) decanoic acid GluA2/GluA3 AMPA receptor antagonism, and Neal et al.'s (2008) randomized childhood epilepsy trial (145 randomized, 103 analyzed at 3 months).

item.title: What an Eye Movement Can Tell Us About Dreaming — Aserinsky & Kleitman's 1953 EOG Awakenings, Dement's Duration Judgments, Foulkes's Definition Shift & Siclari's Posterior Hot Zone
item.description: From Aserinsky & Kleitman's (1953) discovery of Rapid Eye Movement sleep and Dement & Kleitman's (1957) 5-vs.-15-minute binary duration judgments to Foulkes's (1962) proof that NREM mental activity depends on definition thresholds and Siclari et al.'s (2017) posterior cortical low-frequency reduction predicting dream experience within both REM and NREM sleep.

item.title: A Sodium Channel for Pain and Smell — Cox's SCN9A (NaV1.7) Nonsense Variants, Patch-Clamp Loss of Current & Weiss's Olfactory Glomerular Synaptic Failure
item.description: How one voltage-gated sodium channel links nociception and olfaction: Cox et al. (2006) biallelic SCN9A (NaV1.7) truncations eliminating pain while sparing touch, and Weiss et al. (2011) dual recordings proving NaV1.7-null olfactory sensory neurons fire odor-evoked action potentials at the soma but fail to trigger synaptic transmission in the olfactory bulb glomerulus.

item.title: How Infants Tune In to Speech — Werker & Tees's 6-to-12-Month Head-Turn Narrowing, Maye's Bimodal vs. Unimodal Distributions, Kuhl's Live-vs.-Video Mandarin & Lytle's Peer Contingency
item.description: Perceptual narrowing in infant speech acquisition: Werker & Tees (1984) preservation of English contrasts alongside loss of non-native Hindi/Salish discrimination by 10–12 months, Maye, Werker & Gerken (2002) statistical bimodal vs. unimodal distribution reshaping, Kuhl, Tsao & Liu (2003) live vs. televised Mandarin tutors, and Lytle, Garcia-Sierra & Kuhl (2018) peer-paired contingent video.

item.title: How Light Sets the Body Clock — Rodless/Coneless Circadian Phase Shifts, Berson's Retrograde SCN Ganglion Cells, Melanopsin Knockout Rescue & Opn4Diphtheria Ablation
item.description: Discovery of intrinsically photosensitive retinal ganglion cells (ipRGCs): Freedman et al. (1999) intact circadian photoentrainment without rods and cones, Berson, Dunn & Takao (2002) intrinsic light responses in SCN-projecting ganglion cells after synaptic isolation, Hattar et al. (2003) triple-knockout loss of entrainment when rods, cones, and melanopsin are removed together, and Güler et al. (2008) ipRGC cell ablation.

item.title: How a Robin Reads the Tilt of a Magnetic Field — Wiltschko's 1972 Horizontal vs. Vertical Coil Flips, Ritz's Radio-Frequency Disruption & Xu's European Robin Cryptochrome 4
item.description: Biophysics of the avian inclination compass: Wiltschko & Wiltschko (1972) proof that European robins read magnetic field line dip angle (poleward vs. equatorward) rather than polarity, Ritz et al. (2004) diagnostic radio-frequency spin resonance disruption, and Xu et al. (2021) transient absorption spectroscopy of purified migratory European robin vs. non-migratory chicken/pigeon Cryptochrome 4.

item.title: Why an Aroma Can Seem to Come from Your Mouth — Rozin's Dual-Olfaction Juice Test, Dalton's Subthreshold Saccharin-Benzaldehyde Integration, Small's Retronasal fMRI & Blankenship's Optogenetics
item.description: Neurobiology of retronasal olfaction and flavor referral: Rozin (1982) dual-sense hypothesis, Dalton et al. (2000) subthreshold benzaldehyde + saccharin integration (28% lower threshold vs. null MSG control), Small et al. (2005) nasal-cannula fMRI showing route-dependent brain activation for identical vapor concentrations, and Blankenship et al. (2019) gustatory cortex requirement for rapid retronasal learning.

item.title: Who Knew What Was in the Box — Epistemic Access, Secret Ritual Objects, Theory-of-Mind Asymmetries & Religious Authority
item.description: Cognitive and anthropological analysis of hidden ritual contents, asymmetrical epistemic access, and how experiments separate ordinary human false-belief reasoning from attributions of supernatural omniscience.

item.title: How the Nose Builds an Odor Code — Buck & Axel's Olfactory Receptor Family, Zhao's Adenoviral I7 Pairing, Malnic's Combinatorial Code & Bozza's Bulb Glomeruli
item.description: Molecular logic of combinatorial olfaction: Buck & Axel (1991) cloning of the odorant receptor superfamily, Zhao et al. (1998) functional pairing of receptor I7 with octanal, Malnic et al. (1999) single-neuron calcium imaging + RT-PCR showing concentration-dependent recruitment (2 to 5 to 8 receptors for bromooctanoic acid), and Bozza et al. (2004) in vivo glomerular synapto-pHluorin maps.

item.title: Can a God Be Fooled? — Developmental False-Belief Tasks, Barrett's Cracker Box, Yukatek Maya Interviews & Omniscience vs. Moral Policing
item.description: Developmental cognitive science of supernatural minds: unexpected-contents false-belief tasks (Barrett et al. 2001; Knight et al. Yukatek Maya; Lane et al. preparedness vs. anthropomorphism) and separating epistemic omniscience from moral policing across development.

item.title: When GABA Pulls Voltage the Other Way — KCC2 Chloride Extrusion, Gramicidin-Perforated Patch Anion Reversal & Microglial BDNF in Neuropathic Pain
item.description: Ionic basis of GABAergic polarity switches: Rivera et al. (1999) KCC2 antisense knockdown in hippocampal neurons, Coull et al. (2003, 2005) gramicidin-perforated patch recordings in spinal lamina I after nerve injury (-72.6 mV to -49.0 mV) driven by microglial BDNF-TrkB signaling, and depolarizing shunting conductance.

item.title: How a Shark Finds a Fish Under Sand — Murray's Ampullae of Lorenzini Recordings, Kalmijn's Agar-Chamber & Dipole Strikes & Sawfish Electrosense
item.description: Experimental proof of passive electroreception in elasmobranchs: Murray (1962) ampullae of Lorenzini nerve recordings, Kalmijn (1971) catshark and skate strikes at agar-screened live plaice vs. polyethylene insulation vs. artificial bioelectric dipoles, and Wueringer et al. (2012) sawfish rostral electrosense.

item.title: A Chemical Signal Comes in Packets — Fatt & Katz Miniature Endplate Potentials, Del Castillo & Katz Poisson Quantal Failures & Heuser-Reese Quick-Freeze Exocytosis
item.description: Statistical and ultrastructural proof of quantal synaptic transmission: Fatt & Katz (1952) spontaneous miniature endplate potentials, del Castillo & Katz (1954) independent quantal content estimates (0.57 by amplitude ratio vs. 0.56 by Poisson failure fraction), and Heuser & Reese (1979) 3–5 ms quick-freeze electron microscopy.

item.title: Why a Chili Pepper Feels Hot — Caterina & Julius's TRPV1 Expression-Cloning Screen, Thermal Activation, Knockout Hyperalgesia & Chicken-Rat Chimeras
item.description: Discovery and dissection of polymodal nociception via TRPV1: Caterina et al. (1997) Fura-2 expression cloning from dorsal root ganglia, physical heat (>43°C) gating of the capsaicin receptor, Caterina et al. (2000) TRPV1-/- loss of inflammatory thermal hyperalgesia, and Jordt & Julius (2002) separation of capsaicin and thermal gating in avian-mammalian chimeras.

item.title: How the Ear Turns Up Its Own Volume — Brownell's Outer Hair Cell Electromotility, Zheng's Prestin Discovery & Dallos's Stiffness-Preserving Knock-In
item.description: Biophysics of the cochlear amplifier: Brownell et al. (1985) voltage-driven length changes in guinea-pig outer hair cells, Zheng et al. (2000) subtractive cloning of prestin (SLC26A5), Liberman et al. (2002) 40–60 dB threshold shift in prestin-/- mice, and Dallos et al. (2008) 499-prestin knock-in separating active motor force from passive axial stiffness.

item.title: How a Bat Measures the Dark — Pierce & Griffin's Ultrasonic Detector, Galambos's Obstacle Course & Simmons's Electronic Echo-Delay Target Illusion
item.description: Experimental discovery of bat echolocation: Pierce & Griffin (1938) ultrasonic heterodyne detector, Griffin & Galambos (1941) reversible sight vs. hearing vs. vocalization blocks, terminal buzz pursuit (1960), and Kick & Simmons (1984) electronic delay-line phantom targets.

item.title: When One Eye Takes the Lead — Wiesel & Hubel's Monocular vs. Binocular Deprivation, Critical Period Timing & Pizzorusso's Perineuronal Net Chondroitinase
item.description: Synaptic competition and critical period closure in visual cortex: Wiesel & Hubel (1963–1970) why monocular suture shifts cortical drive (1/84 cells) while binocular suture preserves responsiveness, and Pizzorusso et al. (2002) extracellular matrix chondroitin sulfate proteoglycan digestion in adult rats.

item.title: The Butterfly That Steers by a Clock — Monarch Phase-Shifted Flight Simulators, Antennal Circadian Clocks & Conflicting Black-vs.-Clear Enamel Inputs
item.description: Neuroethology of the monarch butterfly time-compensated sun compass: Mouritsen & Frost (2002) ±6h photoperiod shifts (225° vs. 136° vs. 335°), Merlin et al. (2009) antennal light-entrained circadian oscillators, and Guerra et al. (2012) rescue of group orientation by amputating a desynchronized black-painted antenna.

item.title: How We Learned to Read a Cell: A Flash in the Dark — Hecht-Shlaer-Pirenne Thresholds (1942), Baylor Single-Rod Suction Pipettes (1979) & cGMP Gating
item.description: On the Shoulders of Giants Historical Teaching Pilot 1: from Hecht, Shlaer & Pirenne's (1942) 5-14 photon human psychophysical threshold to Baylor, Lamb & Yau's (1979) 1 pA single-photon suction-pipette recordings in toad rod outer segments and Fesenko et al.'s (1985) inside-out patch cGMP gating proof.

item.title: How We Learned to Read a Cell: How a Touch Becomes a Current — Chick Muscle Stretch Channels (1984), Piezo1/2 RNAi Screen (2010) & Bilayer Reconstitution
item.description: On the Shoulders of Giants Historical Teaching Pilot 3: how Guharay & Sachs (1984), Coste et al. (2010, 2012), Ranade et al. (2014), and Syeda et al. (2016) proved that Piezo1 and Piezo2 are the bona fide pore-forming mechanosensitive ion channels underlying vertebrate gentle touch.

item.title: When Stroke Steals Words vs. Meaning — Broca's 'Tan,' Sign-Language Aphasia & Inner Silence
item.description: Traces Broca's 1861 autopsy of Leborgne (and 2007 3T MRI re-scanning), Salk Institute ASL stroke dissociations, corollary discharge, and anendophasia.

item.title: Julian Jaynes on Trial — Did Bronze Age Humans Hear Gods Before Inventing 'I'?
item.description: Puts Julian Jaynes's 1976 Bicameral Mind hypothesis on philological and neurobiological trial against Homeric Greek, Middle Kingdom papyri, and corollary-discharge fMRI.

item.title: Ghosts in the Cortical Map — Civil War Phantoms, Penfield's Probe & Mirror Boxes
item.description: From S. Weir Mitchell's Gettysburg amputees and Wilder Penfield's awake cortical mapping to Ramachandran's mirror box, aplasic phantoms, and somatoparaphrenia.

item.title: Seven Seconds of Now — Patient H.M., Clive Wearing & How Memory Stitches Time
item.description: Unpacks Henry Molaison's 1953 medial temporal resection, Brenda Milner's mirror-star dissociation, Clive Wearing's 7-second diary, and hippocampal time cells.

item.title: The Dreaming Brain Unparalyzed — REM Behavior Disorder & Two-Way Lucid Signals
item.description: From Michel Jouvet's pontine atonia switch and Schenck's REM Behavior Disorder alpha-synuclein prodrome to real-time eye-signal dialogues inside verified REM sleep.

item.title: Where Does Pain Actually Live? — Anzio Beachhead, Nav1.7 & Predictive Interoception
item.description: Debates peripheral nociceptive specificity (Nav1.7 SCN9A) vs. top-down insular predictive interoception (Beecher at Anzio, 1995 boot-nail case, naloxone placebo blockade).

item.title: Before the Brain Had a Name — Egyptian Hearts, Aristotle's Radiator & Herophilus
item.description: How humanity spent 2,000 years locating mind in the heart or diaphragm—from Edwin Smith's trauma papyrus to Aristotle, Herophilus in Alexandria, and Galen's laryngeal pig.

item.title: Wine-Dark Seas & Unspeakable Odors — How Language Shapes Color, Smell & Bedside Pain
item.description: From Gladstone's 1858 shock over Homer's color words and Berlin & Kay's hierarchy to Jahai abstract odor vocabulary and cross-cultural bedside pain ideophones.

item.title: Babylonian Neurology vs. Cos — Esagil-kin-apli's 1050 BCE Seizure Tablet & Hippocrates
item.description: Reads Neo-Babylonian Sakikkū Tablet XXVI (~1050 BCE) side-by-side with Hippocrates's On the Sacred Disease (~400 BCE): Jacksonian marches, auras, and post-ictal paresis.

item.title: Dream Surgery at Epidaurus — Asclepian Sleep Temples, Sacred Snakes & Placebo Neurobiology
item.description: Walks into the 4th-century BCE abaton at Epidaurus—translating the carved Iamata stelae alongside archaeological scalpels and modern PAG opioid/CB1 imaging.

item.title: Alkaline Lithium Springs & Unchained Asylums — Soranus of Ephesus & Humane Roman Psychiatry
item.description: How Soranus of Ephesus (~100 CE) condemned chains, darkness, and the 'wandering womb' myth while prescribing cognitive rehabilitation and lithium-rich alkaline waters.

item.title: Strasbourg 1518 & the Dancing Plagues — Rye Ergot Alkaloids vs. Mass Motor Contagion
